steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Read-through: first reading for overall story, second for character detail, third for design and staging ideas.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Extract the given circumstances: time, place, relationships, events before the play — these are the facts you cannot change.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Identify key moments: turning points, climaxes, revelations — these must be performed with the greatest precision.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Director's concept: the overall vision that shapes every choice — why THIS play NOW? What is the central idea?

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe the process you would use to analyse a script before beginning rehearsals. | What is a director's concept and why is it essential for a coherent production? | How would you identify and prepare for the key moments in a scene from a play you have studied?

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Script work begins with ANALYSIS, not rehearsal The director's concept must be clear BEFORE practical choices are made Key moments must be IDENTIFIED and then HIGHLIGHTED in performance Always consider the PLAYWRIGHT'S intentions alongside your own interpretation
